facts.claim: Option 4. Option 1 fails because the clause is limited to public property. Option 2 fails because Article 300A (in Part XII, inserted by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978) is a constitutional right: no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law; it limits the State and is neither a Fundamental Right nor a duty. Option 3 fails because Article 51A(i) does refer to public property. Damage to private houses is dealt with by ordinary criminal law, not Article 51A.

facts.claim: Option 1 (A–3, B–4, C–1, D–2). B: 'Population control and family planning' is Entry 20A of the Concurrent List, inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976; it is a legislative subject, not a duty in Article 51A. C: Article 46 (Directive Principle) directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, especially SCs and STs. D: Article 51A(g) is the only genuine Fundamental Duty in List I: protect and improve the natural environment and have compassion for living creatures. Option 2 swaps Articles 41 and 46. Option 3 swaps the Concurrent List entry and 51A(g). Option 4 swaps Article 41 and Entry 20A. Rule: three of these four 'welfare' items are State functions (Part IV or Seventh Schedule), not citizens' duties.
